entries.sanskrit:
श्री-गुरुं परमानन्दं वन्द आनन्द-विग्रहम् ।

यस्य सन्नति-मात्रेण चिद् आनन्दायते बपुः ॥

जयन्ति श्री-परानन्द-कृषापाङ्ग-लसद्-दृशः ।

या नित्यम् अनुवर्तन्ते संपदो विगतादृशः ॥

उक्तस् त्रयोदशाध्यायैर् द्वादशे त्व् आश्रयः सतः ।

अधिष्ठानावधित्वाभ्याम् आश्रयश् चेश्वरः सतः ॥

उक्तो लयावधित्वेन प्राकृतात्यन्तिके लये ।

अधिष्ठानतया चोक्तो महा-पुरुष-वर्णने ॥

तत्रादौ षड्भिर् अध्यायैः शुकः प्राह परीक्षिते ।

शेषैस् तत्राखिलान्य् आह सूतः पृष्टोऽथ सत्रिभिः ॥

स्वाश्रय-श्रवणे कार्यो न विलम्बो मनीषिणा ।

इत्य् एतत् काल-वैषम्यं चतुर्भिस् तावद् उच्यते ॥

तत्र तु प्रथमे भावि- मागधान्वय-भूमि-पान् ।

कलि-प्रभावतः प्राह सङ्करादिम् अलीमसान् ॥

तद् एवं वैवस्वत-मनु-वंशे सोम-वंश-प्रस्तावेन श्री-कृष्णावतार-चरितानि स-प्रपञ्चमनुवर्णितानि, अथेदानीं भावी सोम-वंशः कलौ विजातीय-सङ्करादिम् अलीमसो वैरङ्य-द्वारा श्री-कृष्णैक-भक्ति-निगमनायानुवर्ण्यते, तत्र तु सोम-वंश-शाखासु चिर-कालानुवर्तितया मागध-वंशोऽनुक्रम्यते, तत्र पूरोर् वंशे उपरिचरो वसुस् तस्य बृहद्-रथस् तस्य जारसन्धस् तस्य सहदेवः पुत्रोऽभूद् इत्य् उक्तं नवम-स्कन्धे । तत्रैव सहदेवान् मार्जारिस् ततः श्रुतश्रवा इत्य्-आदयो रिपुञ्जयान्ता विंशतिर् भाविनो राजानो निरूपिताः । (तत्र राजा पृच्छति, स्वधामेति । इदानीं) ॥१॥
entries.main_sanskrit: कस्य वंशोऽभवत् पृथ्व्याम् एतद् आचक्ष्व मे मुने ॥
word_for_word: the refuge of the existent world
entries.literal_english: I bow to the supremely blissful Guru, the embodiment of bliss, by whose mere prostration the body becomes consciousness-bliss. May the shining glances of Śrī Parānanda Kṛṣṇa, whose compassion-filled sidelong eyes gleam, triumph; they are followed eternally by spiritual wealth, beyond the reach of ordinary sight. The refuge of the existent world is the Lord, as stated in the thirteen chapters of this Canto; he is its refuge both as the limit of dissolution and as its foundation. He is the limit in material and final dissolution, and he is declared the foundation in the description of the Supreme Person. In the first six chapters Śuka spoke to Parīkṣit; in the remaining chapters Sūta, questioned by the sages, tells all the desired accounts. A wise person should not delay in hearing the Lord who is his refuge. This time-disorder is explained first in four chapters. Here, in the first, the future rulers of the Magadha line are described as stained by social mixture and other faults under the influence of Kali. Thus, after the accounts of Kṛṣṇa’s incarnation in the Vaivasvata Manu and lunar dynasties, the future lunar line is now described as corrupted in Kali, so that its degradation may lead, through detachment, to the conclusion that exclusive devotion to Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the sole means. The Magadha line is traced because it continued for a long time among the branches of the lunar dynasty: in the line of Pūru, Uparicara Vasu was followed by Bṛhadratha, Jarāsandha and Sahadeva, as stated in the Ninth Canto. There too, twenty future kings—from Sahadeva through Mārgāri, Śrutaśravā and the line ending in Ripuñjaya—were described. Here the king asks, beginning with ‘after Kṛṣṇa had returned to his abode.’

entries.sanskrit: तद्-उपरितनं वंशं सङ्करादि-दोषैः प्रपञ्चयति—योऽन्त्य इति । रिपुञ्जय एव पुरञ्जयः । स्वामिनं पुरञ्जयं हत्वा स्व-पुत्रं प्रद्योत-संज्ञं राजानं करिष्यति । यस्य पालको नाम सुतो भविष्यति ॥२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यामात्यस् तु शुनको हत्वा स्वामिनम् आत्म-जम् ॥

प्रद्योत-संज्ञं राजानं कर्ता यत्-पालकः सुतः ।
word_for_word: with faults beginning with social mixture
entries.literal_english: He elaborates the lineage above this, with faults beginning with social mixture: ‘the last one.’ Ripuñjaya himself is Purañjaya. After killing his master Purañjaya, Śunaka will make his own son, named Pradyota, king. His son will be named Pālaka.

tasyāmātyas tu śunako hatvā svāminam ātma-jam ||

pradyota-saṃjñaṃ rājānaṃ kartā yat-pālakaḥ sutaḥ |

entries.sanskrit: प्रद्योतनाः प्रद्योत-संज्ञाः ॥४॥
entries.main_sanskrit: अष्ट-त्रिंशोत्तर-शतं भोक्ष्यन्ति पृथिवीं नृपाः ॥
entries.literal_english: The Pradyotanas are those named Pradyota.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्षेमधर्मा तस्य सुतः क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेमधर्म-जः ॥

विधिसारः सुतस् तस्या- जातशत्रुर् भविष्यति ।

शिशुनागा दशैवैते षष्ट्य्-उत्तर-शत-त्रयम् ॥

समा भोक्ष्यन्ति पृथिवीं कुरु-श्रेष्ठ कलौ नृपाः ।

ततः प्रद्योतनेभ्यः पश्चात् । भाव्यो भविष्यति । तत्सुतः शिशुनागः सुतः । तस्य काकवर्णस्य ॥ तस्य क्षेत्रज्ञस्य, तस्य अजातशत्रुः, तस्येत्युभयान्वयि । तत्सुतोऽजातशत्रुसुतः ॥ आजेयोऽजयपुत्रः । अत्रैकारमध्यत्वमार्षम् । ततो नन्दिवर्द्धनस्य । षष्ट्युत्तरशतत्रयं ३६० राज्यभोगवर्षसङ्ख्येयम् ॥५-८॥

kṣemadharmā tasya sutaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ kṣemadharma-jaḥ ||

vidhisāraḥ sutas tasyā- jātaśatrur bhaviṣyati |

śiśunāgā daśaivaite ṣaṣṭy-uttara-śata-trayam ||

entries.sanskrit: नन्दो नाम कश्चिन् महा-पद्म-सङ्ख्याया सेनायाः धनस्य वा पतिर् भविष्यति । अत एव महा-पद्म इत्य् अपि तस्य नाम ॥९॥
entries.main_sanskrit: ततो नृपा भविष्यन्ति शूद्र-प्रायास् त्व् अधार्मिकाः ॥
word_for_word: of an army counted in mahāpadmas
entries.literal_english: A certain Nanda will become the lord of an army or wealth measured in mahāpadmas; therefore Mahāpadma is also his name.

entries.sanskrit: एकम् एव छत्रं यस्यां तां पृथिवीं शासिष्यति पालयिष्यति । क्षत्रोत्सादने दृष्टान्तः, भार्गवः परशुराम इव ॥१०॥
entries.main_sanskrit: शासिष्यति महापद्मो द्वितीय इव भार्गवः ॥
word_for_word: in the destruction of the kṣatriyas
entries.literal_english: He will rule and protect the earth under a single parasol. The example for the destruction of the kṣatriyas is Bhārgava Paraśurāma.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: śāsiṣyati mahāpadmo dvitīya iva bhārgavaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: समाः संवत्सरान् ॥११॥ नव नन्दान् नन्दं च तत्-पुत्रांश् चेत्य् एवं नव । प्रपन्नान् विश्वस् तान् विख्यातान् वा । द्विजः कौटिल्य-वात्स्यायनादि-पर्यायश् चाणक्य उद्धरिष्यत्य् उन्मूलयिष्यति । मौर्या मौर्य-संज्ञाः ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
य इमां भोक्ष्यन्ति महीं राजानश् च शतं समाः ॥

नव नन्दान् द्विजः कश्चित् प्रपन्नान् उद्धरिष्यति ।
entries.literal_english: ‘Years’ means solar years. ‘The nine Nandas’ means Nanda together with his sons, making nine. ‘Trusting’ means trusted, or famous. The brāhmaṇa is Cāṇakya, also known by the names Kauṭilya and Vātsyāyana; he will uproot them. The Mauryas are those bearing the name Maurya.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
ya imāṃ bhokṣyanti mahīṃ rājānaś ca śataṃ samāḥ ||

nava nandān dvijaḥ kaścit prapannān uddhariṣyati |

entries.sanskrit: कथं भोक्ष्यन्ति तद् आह—स एवेति । चन्द्रगुप्तं मौर्य-प्रथमम् ॥१३॥
entries.main_sanskrit: तत्-सुतो वारिसारस् तु ततश् चाशोकवर्धनः ॥
entries.literal_english: How will they rule? He explains: ‘he himself.’ This refers to Candragupta, the first Maurya.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: tat-suto vārisāras tu tataś cāśokavardhanaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
सुयशा भविता तस्य सङ्गतः सुयशः-सुतः ।

शालिशूकस् ततस् तस्य सोमशर्मा भविष्यति ।

शतधन्वा ततस् तस्य भविता तद् बृहद्रथः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.

entries.transliteration:
suyaśā bhavitā tasya saṅgataḥ suyaśaḥ-sutaḥ |

śāliśūkas tatas tasya somaśarmā bhaviṣyati |

śatadhanvā tatas tasya bhavitā tad bṛhadrathaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: तेषां पञ्चमो दशरथः पारशरादिभिर् उक्तोऽत्राप्य् अनुसन्धेयः । तेन सह मौर्या दश । सप्त-त्रिंशच्-छतोत्तरं सप्त-त्रिंशद्-उत्तरं शतं समाः ॥१५॥
entries.main_sanskrit: समा भोक्ष्यन्ति पृथिवीं कलौ कुरु-कुलोद्वह ॥
entries.literal_english: The fifth of them, Daśaratha, is stated by Parāśara and others and should also be connected here. Including him, there are ten Mauryas. The figure is one hundred and thirty-seven years.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: samā bhokṣyanti pṛthivīṃ kalau kuru-kulodvaha ||

entries.sanskrit: बृहद्-रथस्य सेनापतिः पुष्यमित्रो नाम स्वामिनं बृहद्-रथं हत्वा राज्यं करिष्यति । स च शुङ्गानां प्रथमः ॥१६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
हत्वा बृहद्-रथं मौर्यं तस्य सेनापतिः कलौ ।

पुष्यमित्रस् तु शुङ्गाह्वः स्वयं राज्यं करिष्यति ॥
entries.literal_english: Puṣyamitra, named as the commander of Bṛhadratha’s army, will kill his master Bṛhadratha and take the kingdom. He is the first of the Śuṅgas.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
hatvā bṛhad-rathaṃ mauryaṃ tasya senāpatiḥ kalau |

puṣyamitras tu śuṅgāhvaḥ svayaṃ rājyaṃ kariṣyati ||

entries.sanskrit: ततोऽग्नि-मित्रादयो नवेत्य् एवं शुङ्गा दश-वर्ष-शताधिकं द्वादशाधिकं वर्ष-शतम् ॥१७-१९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अग्निमित्रस् ततस् तस्मात् सुज्येष्ठो भविता ततः ।

वसुमित्रो भद्रकश् च पुलिन्दो भविता सुतः ॥

ततो घोषः सुतस् तस्माद् वज्रमित्रो भविष्यति ।

ततो भागवतस् तस्माद् देवभूतिः कुरूद्वह ॥

शुङ्गा दशैते भोक्ष्यन्ति भूमिं वर्ष-शताधिकम् ।

ततः काण्वान् इयं भूमिर् यास्यत्य् अल्प-गुणान् नृप ॥
entries.transliteration:
agnimitras tatas tasmāt sujyeṣṭho bhavitā tataḥ |

vasumitro bhadrakaś ca pulindo bhavitā sutaḥ ||

tato ghoṣaḥ sutas tasmād vajramitro bhaviṣyati |

tato bhāgavatas tasmād devabhūtiḥ kurūdvaha ||

śuṅgā daśaite bhokṣyanti bhūmiṃ varṣa-śatādhikam |

tataḥ kāṇvān iyaṃ bhūmir yāsyaty alpa-guṇān nṛpa ||
entries.literal_english: After Puṣyamitra came Agnimitra and the other nine Śuṅga kings. These ten ruled the earth for more than a hundred years—twelve years beyond a hundred—after which the earth would pass to the Kāṇvas, kings of lesser qualities.

entries.sanskrit: कथं कण्वान् यास्यति ? तद् आह—शुङ्गम् इति । पर-स्त्री-कामिनं देवभूति-नामानं शुङ्गं हत्वा तद्-अमात्यो वसुदेव-नामा कण्वो राज्यं करिष्यति ॥२०॥
entries.main_sanskrit: स्वयं करिष्यते राज्यं वसुदेवो महा-मतिः ॥
word_for_word: how will he pass to the Kāṇvas
entries.literal_english: How will he pass to the Kāṇvas? He explains: ‘the Śuṅga.’ Vasudeva, a Kāṇva named as his minister, will kill the lustful Śuṅga named Devabhūti and take the kingdom.

entries.sanskrit: काण्वानां चतुर्थः सुशर्मा ज्ञेयः ॥२१॥
entries.main_sanskrit: नारायणस्य भविता सुशर्मा नाम विश्रुतः ॥
entries.literal_english: Suśarmā is to be understood as the fourth of the Kāṇvas.

entries.transliteration: nārāyaṇasya bhavitā suśarmā nāma viśrutaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: इमे वसुदेवादयः काण्वायना वर्षाणां त्रीणि शतानि पञ्च-चत्वारिंशद्-वर्षाणि च भूमिं भोक्ष्यन्ति ॥२२॥
entries.main_sanskrit: शतानि त्रीणि भोक्ष्यन्ति वर्षाणां च कलौ युगे ॥
entries.literal_english: These Kāṇvāyanas, beginning with Vasudeva, will rule the earth for three hundred and forty-five years.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: śatāni trīṇi bhokṣyanti varṣāṇāṃ ca kalau yuge ||

entries.sanskrit: काण्वानाम् अन्तिमं सुशर्माणं हत्वा बली-नामा तद् भृत्यो गां भोक्ष्यति ॥२३॥
entries.main_sanskrit: गां भोक्ष्यत्य् अन्ध्र-जातीयः कञ्चित् कालम् असत्तमः ॥
entries.literal_english: After killing Suśarmā, the last of the Kāṇvas, his servant named Balī, a powerful man, will rule the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: gāṃ bhokṣyaty andhra-jātīyaḥ kañcit kālam asattamaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्री-शान्तकर्णस् तत्-पुत्रः पौर्णमासस् तु तत्-सुतः ॥

लम्बोदरस् तु तत्-पुत्रस् तस्माच् चिबिलको नृपः ।

पुरीषभीरुस् तत्-पुत्रस् ततो राजा सुनन्दनः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
śrī-śāntakarṇas tat-putraḥ paurṇamāsas tu tat-sutaḥ ||

lambodaras tu tat-putras tasmāc cibilako nṛpaḥ |

purīṣabhīrus tat-putras tato rājā sunandanaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: यत्र येषु बहु-संज्ञेष्व् अष्टसु चरमः शिवस्वाति-नामा भविता ॥२७॥
entries.main_sanskrit: तस्यापि गोमती पुत्रः पुरीमान् भविता ततः ॥
entries.literal_english: Among those eight, in the places bearing many names, the last will be named Śivasvāti.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: tasyāpi gomatī putraḥ purīmān bhavitā tataḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
विजयस् तत्-सुतो भाव्यश् चन्द्रविज्ञः स-लोमधिः ॥

एते त्रिंशन् नृपतयश् चत्वार्य् अब्द-शतानि च ।
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
vijayas tat-suto bhāvyaś candravijñaḥ sa-lomadhiḥ ||

ete triṃśan nṛpatayaś catvāry abda-śatāni ca |

entries.sanskrit: आवभृत्याः अवभृतिर् नगरी तद् राजानः ॥३०॥
entries.main_sanskrit: कङ्काः षोडश भू-पाला भविष्यन्त्य् अति-लोलुपाः ॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Āvabhṛtyas’ means the kings of the city named Āvabhṛti.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: kaṅkāḥ ṣoḍaśa bhū-pālā bhaviṣyanty ati-lolupāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
ततोऽष्टौ यवना भाव्याश् चतुर्दश तुरुष्ककाः ।

भूयो दश गुरुण्डाश् च मौला एकादशैव तु ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
tato’ṣṭau yavanā bhāvyāś caturdaśa turuṣkakāḥ |

bhūyo daśa guruṇḍāś ca maulā ekādaśaiva tu ||

entries.sanskrit:
एते आभीरादयो मौल-व्यतिरिक्ताः पञ्च-षष्टि-नृपा एकोन-शताधिकं वर्ष-सहस्रं पृथिवीं भोक्ष्यन्ति । ततः पूर्वोक्ता एवैकादश मौलास् त्रीण्य् अब्द-शतानि क्षितिं भोक्ष्यन्ति ॥३२॥ 

तैः संस्थिते तेषु मृतेषु किलिकिलायां पुर्यां नृपतयो भविष्यन्तीत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥३३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
नवाधिकां च नवतिं मौला एकादश क्षितिम् ॥

भोक्ष्यन्त्य् अब्द-शतान्य् अङ्ग त्रीणि तैः संस्थिते ततः ।
entries.literal_english: These sixty-five kings, apart from the Maulas, will rule the earth for one thousand and ninety-nine years. Then the eleven Maulas mentioned earlier will rule the earth for three hundred years. After they have established themselves and died, kings will arise in the city of Kilikilā; this is the connection with what follows.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
navādhikāṃ ca navatiṃ maulā ekādaśa kṣitim ||

bhokṣyanty abda-śatāny aṅga trīṇi taiḥ saṃsthite tataḥ |

entries.sanskrit: अधिकानि षड्-वर्षाणि च ॥३४॥
entries.main_sanskrit: इत्य् एते वै वर्ष-शतं भविष्यन्त्य् अधिकानि षट् ॥
entries.literal_english: And six additional years.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: ity ete vai varṣa-śataṃ bhaviṣyanty adhikāni ṣaṭ ||

entries.sanskrit:
तेषां भूतनन्दादीनां यथा-यथं बाह्लिक-नामानस् त्रयोदश सुता भविष्यन्ति । अथ पुष्पमित्रो नामान्यो राजन्यः । अस्य च दुर्मित्रो नाम पुत्रः ॥३५॥

तथा आन्ध्राः कोशला विदूर-पतयो निषधाश् च एते च तत् तद् देश-नामभिः प्रख्यातास् तुल्य-कालाः खण्ड-मण्डलेषु भूपास् तत एव तेभ्यो बाह्लिकेभ्य एव भाव्या भविष्यन्ति ॥३६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पुष्पमित्रोऽथ राजन्यो दुर्मित्रोऽस्य तथैव च ॥

एक-काला इमे भू-पाः सप्तान्ध्राः सप्त कौशलाः ।
word_for_word: by the names of their respective countries
entries.literal_english: Thirteen sons of those kings beginning with Bhūtananda will successively bear the name Bāhlika. Then there will be another king named Puṣpamitra, and his son will be named Durmitra. Likewise the Andhras, Kauśalas, rulers of Vidūra and Niṣadhas—known by the names of their respective countries—will be kings of separate districts ruling at the same time; they too will arise from those Bāhlikas.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
puṣpamitro’tha rājanyo durmitro’sya tathaiva ca ||

eka-kālā ime bhū-pāḥ saptāndhrāḥ sapta kauśalāḥ |

entries.sanskrit: ततश् च मागधानां तु राजा विश्वस्फूर्जिर् नाम भविता । स चापूर्वोक्तात् पुरञ्जयाद् अपरः पुरञ्जय इति प्रसिद्धः सन् वर्णान् ब्राह्मणादीन् पुलिन्द-यदु-मद्रक-संज्ञान् म्लेच्छ-प्रायान् करिष्यति । अपरान् इति पाठे अन्यान् पुलिन्दादि-संज्ञान् वर्णान् करिष्यतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३७॥
entries.main_sanskrit: करिष्यत्य् अपरो वर्णान् पुलिन्द-यदु-मद्रकान् ॥
entries.literal_english: Then a king of Magadha named Viśvasphūrji will appear. He will be another Purañjaya, famous as a Purañjaya different from the one mentioned earlier, and he will turn the civilized classes—brāhmaṇas and the others—into outcastes known as Pulindas, Yadus and Madrakas, almost mlecchas. If the reading is ‘aparān,’ the meaning is that he will make other classes bear the names Pulinda and the like.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration: kariṣyaty aparo varṇān pulinda-yadu-madrakān ||

entries.sanskrit: किं चैवं कृत्वाब्रह्म-भूयिष्ठा अत्रैवर्ण्याप्रचुराः सतीः प्रजाः स्थापयिष्यति पालयिष्यति । स च पद्मवत्यां पुरि वसन् अनुगङ्गां गङ्गा-द्वारम् आरभ्य प्रयाग-पर्यन्तं गुप्तां पालितां मेदिनीं भोक्ष्यति ॥३८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
वीर्यवान् क्षत्रम् उत्साद्य पद्मवत्यां स वै पुरी ॥

अनु-गङ्गम् आ-प्रयागं गुप्तां भोक्ष्यति मेदिनीम्
entries.literal_english: Having done this, he will establish and protect populations that are predominantly non-Brahminical. Residing in the city of Padmavatī, he will rule the earth protected from Gaṅgādvāra, the gateway of the Gaṅgā, as far as Prayāga.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
vīryavān kṣatram utsādya padmavatyāṃ sa vai purī ||

anu-gaṅgam ā-prayāgaṃ guptāṃ bhokṣyati medinīm

entries.sanskrit: तद्-अनन्तरं च सौराष्ट्रादि-देश-वर्तिनो द्विजा व्रात्या उपनयन-रहिता भविष्यन्ति ॥३९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सौराष्ट्रावन्त्य्-आभीराश् च शूरा अर्बुद-मालवाः ।
व्रात्या द्विजा भविष्यन्ति शूद्र-प्राया जनाधिपाः ॥
entries.literal_english: After that, the brāhmaṇas living in the countries beginning with Saurāṣṭra will become vratyas, without the upanayana initiation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
saurāṣṭrāvanty-ābhīrāś ca śūrā arbuda-mālavāḥ |
vrātyā dvijā bhaviṣyanti śūdra-prāyā janādhipāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अब्रह्म-वर्चसो वेदाचार-शून्याः ॥४०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सिन्धोस् तटं चन्द्रभागां कौन्तीं काश्मीर-मण्डलम् ।
भोक्ष्यन्ति शूद्रा व्रात्याद्या म्लेच्छाश् चाब्रह्म-वर्चसः ॥
entries.literal_english: Without Brahmanical radiance, they will be devoid of Vedic practice.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
sindhos taṭaṃ candrabhāgāṃ kauntīṃ kāśmīra-maṇḍalam |
bhokṣyanti śūdrā vrātyādyā mlecchāś cābrahma-varcasaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: इमे च म्लेच्छ-प्राया भूभृतस् तुल्य-काला भविष्यन्ति । किं च, एते सर्वेऽधर्मानृत-परा अधर्मेऽनृते च परिनिष्ठिताः फल्गु-दा अल्प-दातारः ॥४१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तुल्य-काला इमे राजन् म्लेच्छ-प्रायाश् च भू-भृतः ।
एतेऽधर्मानृत-पराः फल्गु-दास् तीव्र-मन्यवः ॥
entries.literal_english: These rulers, mostly mlecchas, will rule at the same time. They will be devoted to irreligion and falsehood, firmly established in them, and will give little benefit, being small or stingy givers.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tulya-kālā ime rājan mleccha-prāyāś ca bhū-bhṛtaḥ |
ete’dharmānṛta-parāḥ phalgu-dās tīvra-manyavaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: उदितास्त-मित-प्राया हर्ष-शोकादि-बहुलाः ॥४२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
स्त्री-बाल-गो-द्विज-घ्नाश् च पर-दार-धनादृताः ।
उदितास्त-मित-प्राया अल्प-सत्त्वाल्पकायुषः ॥
word_for_word: mostly subject to rising and setting
abundant in joy, grief and the like
entries.literal_english: They will be mostly subject to rising and setting, with abundant joy, grief and the like.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
strī-bāla-go-dvija-ghnāś ca para-dāra-dhanādṛtāḥ |
uditāsta-mita-prāyā alpa-sattvālpakāyuṣaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: असंस्कृता गर्भाधानादि-संस्कार-रहिताः । प्रजा भक्षयिष्यन्ति धनाद्य्-अपहारादिना पीडयिष्यन्ति ॥४३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
असंस्कृताः क्रिया-हीना रजसा तमसावृताः ।
प्रजास् ते भक्षयिष्यन्ति म्लेच्छा राजन्य-रूपिणः ॥
word_for_word: taking away wealth and the like
entries.literal_english: Uncultured means without the purificatory rites beginning with conception. They will devour the citizens—afflicting them by taking away wealth and the like.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
asaṃskṛtāḥ kriyā-hīnā rajasā tamasāvṛtāḥ |
prajās te bhakṣayiṣyanti mlecchā rājanya-rūpiṇaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: किं च, तन्-नाथाः ते नाथा येषां ते जनपदा देश-वर्तिनो मनुष्यास् तच्-छीलाचार-वादिनस् तेषाम् इव शीलम् आचारो वादश् च तद्वन्तः ॥४४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तन्-नाथास् ते जनपदास् तच्-छीलाचार-वादिनः ।
अन्योन्यतो राजभिश् च क्षयं यास्यन्ति पीडिताः ॥
entries.literal_english: Moreover, the provinces whose lords they are, and the people living in those countries, will possess their character, conduct and speech, imitating them in these respects.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tan-nāthās te janapadās tac-chīlācāra-vādinaḥ |
anyonyato rājabhiś ca kṣayaṃ yāsyanti pīḍitāḥ ||
